name: Dynamics of Human Relationships
subject: Social Sciences and Humanities
description: This course focuses on helping students understand the individual and group factors that contribute to healthy relationships. Students will examine the connections between their own self-concept and their interpersonal relationships. They will learn and practise strategies for developing and maintaining healthy relationships with friends, family, and community members, as well as with partners in intimate relationships. Students will use research and inquiry skills to investigate topics related to healthy relationships.

strands.title: Rights and Responsibilities
strands.describer: By the end of this course, students will:

overall_expectations.title: Individual Rights and Responsibilities
overall_expectations.describer: By the end of this course, students will:
overall_expectations.text: demonstrate an understanding of the nature of individual rights and responsibilities in human interactions
overall_expectations.text_html: demonstrate an understanding of the nature of individual rights and responsibilities in human interactions

specific_expectations.text: identify the rights of the individual in human interactions as outlined in a variety of laws and policies (e.g., the Ontario Human Rights Code, the Employment Standards Act, the Ontario Environmental Bill of Rights, the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, the Indian Act, the Privacy Act, the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights)
specific_expectations.text_html: identify the rights of the individual in human interactions as outlined in a variety of laws and policies (e.g., the Ontario Human Rights Code, the Employment Standards Act, the Ontario Environmental Bill of Rights, the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, the Indian Act, the Privacy Act, the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights)

elaborations.text:
Why is legislation important in governing human interactions?
  What are the protected grounds in the Ontario Human Rights Code?
  In a high school setting, what are the implications of the fact that sexual orientation, gender identity, and gender expression are protected grounds in the Ontario Human Rights Code?
  What protections does the Ontario Environmental Bill of Rights give to individuals?
elaborations.text_html:
• Why is legislation important in governing human interactions?
  • What are the protected grounds in the Ontario Human Rights Code?

specific_expectations.text: identify the individual’s responsibilities in human interactions (e.g., obeying Canada’s laws, refraining from infringing on the rights of others, promoting respect for others, encouraging the responsible use of technology)
specific_expectations.text_html: identify the individual’s responsibilities in human interactions (e.g., obeying Canada’s laws, refraining from infringing on the rights of others, promoting respect for others, encouraging the responsible use of technology)

overall_expectations.text_html: demonstrate an understanding of the extent of individual rights and responsibilities within the wider community
